ls.story.intro1.text: Budge has a big dream: a telescope to see the stars.

ls.story.intro2.text: So Budge opens a lemonade stand on the beach!

ls.story.intro3.text: First she has to buy lemons, and then sell lots of cups.

ls.story.intro4.text: Can you help Budge count the money?

ls.story.between2.text: The first customers are smiling. Sip, sip!

ls.story.between4.text: Budge's money jar is filling up.

ls.story.between6.text: Clouds are coming. Will people still buy lemonade?

ls.story.outro1.text: What a day at the stand!

ls.story.outro2.text: You counted coins carefully and worked out the profit.

ls.story.outro3.text: Budge is closer to her telescope. Here's your Stand Star!

ls.prompt.tutorial.text: A lemon costs 3 cents. Put 3 pennies on the counter, then tap Pay!

ls.prompt.pay1.text: A lemon costs {c} cents. Pay the farmer!

ls.prompt.pay2.text: A bag of lemons costs {c} cents. Pay the farmer!

ls.prompt.pay.dollar.text: A big bag of lemons costs one dollar. Pay the farmer!

ls.prompt.change.text: Bobbo pays one dollar for a {c} cent cup. Give him his change!

ls.prompt.cost.text: Move the supplies into the stand. What does one batch cost?

ls.prompt.revenue.text: Serve {n} cups at {c} cents each. How much money came in?

ls.prompt.revenue.dollar.text: Serve {n} cups at one dollar each. How much money came in?

ls.prompt.profit.text: What profit did Budge make? Save it in her jar!

ls.prompt.loss.text: Rainy day! Was it a profit or a loss? How much?

ls.prompt.price.text: Slide the price. Which price makes the most profit?

ls.help.value.text: Count the value, not the number of coins. One dime is worth two nickels.

ls.help.big-first.text: Start with the biggest coins, then add smaller ones.

ls.help.count-up.text: To give change, count up from the price to one dollar.

ls.help.cost.text: Cost is what Budge spends to make the lemonade.

ls.help.revenue.text: Revenue is all the money from selling: cups times price.

ls.help.profit.text: Profit is what's left after paying the costs.

ls.help.price.text: A higher price means fewer cups sold. Find the best mix.

ls.help.not-price.text: That's the price of the cup. Change is the rest, up to one dollar.

ls.help.all-three.text: Remember every supply: lemons, sugar and cups.

ls.help.times.text: Each cup brings in the price. Add the price once for every cup.

ls.help.take-away.text: Costs are taken away from the money that came in, not added.

ls.help.loss.text: When supplies cost more than the money that came in, that's a loss.

ls.help.most-cups.text: Selling the most cups isn't always best. Each cup earns its price minus its cost.

ls.praise.1.text: You counted the value of every coin!

ls.praise.2.text: Counting up gave the right change.

ls.praise.3.text: You remembered to take away the costs.

ls.praise.4.text: You compared every price before choosing.

ls.praise.5.text: Biggest coins first. What a tidy way to pay!

ls.praise.6.text: You added up every supply. That's the cost of a batch!

ls.praise.7.text: Cups times price. You worked out the revenue!

ls.retry.1.text: Not quite yet. Let's look again.

ls.hint.modelTap.text: Now you try. Tap the glowing button.

ls.idle.text: Drag or tap the glowing things to help Budge.

ls.supplies.in.text: All the supplies are in the stand!

ls.served.text: Everyone has a cup of lemonade!
